title: Optimized Pre-Processing for Discrimination Prevention
abstract: Non-discrimination is a recognized objective in algorithmic decision making. In this paper, we introduce a novel probabilistic formulation of data pre-processing for reducing discrimination. We propose a convex optimization for learning a data transformation with three goals: controlling discrimination, limiting distortion in individual data samples, and preserving utility. We characterize the impact of limited sample size in accomplishing this objective. Two instances of the proposed optimization are applied to datasets, including one on real-world criminal recidivism. Results show that discrimination can be greatly reduced at a small cost in classification accuracy.

claims.text: A probabilistic formulation of data pre-processing can be used to reduce discrimination in algorithmic decision making.
Convex optimization can learn a data transformation that simultaneously controls discrimination, limits sample distortion, and preserves utility.
Limited sample size impacts the ability of optimized pre-processing to prevent discrimination.
Data discrimination can be significantly reduced at a small cost in classification accuracy.

limitations.text: The efficacy of the discrimination prevention optimization is constrained by limited sample sizes.

methodologies.name: Probabilistic Convex Optimization Pre-Processing
methodologies.description: A convex optimization framework for learning probabilistic data transformations that balance discrimination control, sample distortion limits, and data utility.
